raw_response:
I farm the way I always have to think about it: first keep the land busy, second don’t spend so much that I get stuck without cash. My family only has 2 people, so 20 mu is already enough work. Wheat and maize are steady for us, they give grain and are less risky. Cabbage can make money, but it needs more hand work and more medicine, and if the price falls fast, you suffer. So I would not put all 20 mu into cabbage even if I know how to grow it. I would keep 12 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, and use 8 mu for three rounds of cabbage. I have a well, so I can water when the crop is dry, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water for nothing. I don’t read books, I just do what has worked on my own land and what other people around here do. Fertilizer, I would rather put a bit more than too little, because if the crop turns weak, the loss is bigger than wasting a little fertilizer.
